Madison County by the numbers

What does the Madison County Judge of Probate do with a deed?

The Madison County Judge of Probate is the office where deeds and mortgages are recorded, and a deed does not give a buyer public notice of ownership until it is filed there. The recording office is at the Madison County Service Center, 1918 Memorial Parkway NW, Huntsville, the same building that houses the tax collector and the Board of Equalization.

Alabama counties handle several jobs that other states split between offices. The probate judge also deals with estates, and in Madison County the probate staff records the documents that move title. The office says plainly that its staff cannot give legal advice, so questions about how to word a deed belong with an attorney or a closing agent.

For a seller, the recording step is the last thing that happens. The title company prepares the deed, collects the recording charges and the deed tax at closing, and files the paperwork.

What are the Madison County recording fees for a deed?

The posted schedule totals $25.75 for the first page of a document and $2.50 for each additional page. The county's own fee page is dated April 1, 2013, so check with the office for any later change before you rely on it for an exact figure.

ChargeAmount
Imaging fee$10.00
Per page$2.50
Filing fee$1.00
Microfilm$0.25
Mental health fee$12.00
Total, first page$25.75
Each additional page$2.50

A three-page deed that carries its own sales validation information would therefore cost $30.75 to record on this schedule, before the deed tax. If a separate validation form is attached, add $2.50 for that page.

How much is the Alabama deed tax in Madison County?

The deed tax is $0.50 for each $500 of value or fraction of $500, which works out to $1.00 per $1,000. Madison County prints it as 50 cents per $500, based on the appraised value or the purchase price, with a minimum of 50 cents if the purchase is 100% financed.

The state statute behind it is section 40-22-1 of the Code of Alabama. It sets the tax at $0.50 for each $500 or fraction in value conveyed, and it taxes only the value above any mortgage or vendor's lien that has already paid mortgage tax. Two thirds of what the probate judge collects goes to the state treasury and one third to the county treasury.

As plain arithmetic from that formula, a sale at $250,000 produces 500 units of $500, so the deed tax is $250. A sale at $180,000 produces 360 units and $180. These are illustrations, not quotes, so your closing agent should run the actual numbers.

Some instruments are exempt. The statute lists transfers of mortgages that already paid mortgage tax, deeds for nominal consideration meant to perfect title, and re-recorded corrected instruments.

What is the RT-1 form and when does Madison County require it?

The RT-1 Real Estate Sales Validation form is required to accompany deeds recorded in Madison County, unless the same information is written into the deed itself. The requirement took effect on August 1, 2012, and the county charges an extra $2.50 page fee when the form is recorded. It does not apply to correction deeds.

State law is the reason. Section 40-22-1 requires proof of the actual purchase price, or the actual value if the property was not sold. The Department of Revenue developed the form, and a person who signs it in good faith is not required to provide more documentation. A person who intentionally refuses to give the proof after a specific request, or gives false proof, owes a penalty of $100 or 25% of the tax due, whichever is greater.

If no proof is offered at all, the probate judge computes the tax from the latest assessment, and the penalty can apply. For sellers, the simplest course is to make sure the settlement statement and the RT-1 show the same price.

What must a document include to be recorded in Madison County?

The county posts a short list of requirements, and a deed that misses one can be rejected at the counter.

  • Original documents are required, and copies from other courts must be certified.
  • Every document must carry the name and address of the person who prepared it.
  • Grantor marital status must appear on all deeds, and mortgagor status on mortgages.
  • Checks are payable to Judge of Probate, Madison County, Alabama.
  • Mailed documents need an adequately sized self-addressed stamped envelope and a 3-inch margin at the top of the first page.

Electronic recording is available through two approved vendors, Simplifile and CSC. E-recording stops at 4 p.m. daily, and the clerks cannot fill in blanks on a document. If two documents have to record in order, such as a deed followed by a second mortgage, the county advises waiting until the first is returned before uploading the next. It also asks you to call before submitting a transaction that spans several counties.

How are names indexed, and what extra charges can appear?

Madison County indexes two grantors, two grantees and two cross-references at no charge, and each additional name or reference costs $1. The county counts more than people toward that limit.

The fee page says the count includes a/k/a and d/b/a names, trusts and trustees, administrators and personal representatives, an estate of a deceased person, MERS, and companies listed as manager, member or partner. An inherited house sold by an estate, or a property owned by an LLC with several managers, can pick up a few of these small charges.

Other items on the posted schedule:

  • Certified copies cost $1 per page plus $2 for certification.
  • Mortgage tax is 15 cents per $100, or $1.50 per $1,000, rounded up to the next $100.
  • Mortgages and deeds to exempt entities carry an additional 50 cent no tax stamp fee.
  • Releases, assignments, affidavits, liens and powers of attorney use the same basic recording fees as deeds.

What changes when a deed and a mortgage are filed together?

When a deed and a mortgage record at the same time, the deed tax is paid on the down payment or equity, not the full price. If the entire price is financed, the deed tax drops to the 50 cent minimum.

The exception is a deed filed with a tax-exempt mortgage, where the deed tax is figured on the full purchase price or appraised value. The county also tells filers to confirm the deed and mortgage consideration in the e-recording system before submitting.

A cash sale is simpler. With no lender, no mortgage tax applies to the buyer's side, and the transaction usually needs only the deed, the validation form and the recording charges.

How does Madison County fit into a Huntsville-area home sale?

Madison County is the second most populous county in Alabama, with 388,153 residents counted in 2020 and about 433,516 estimated for 2025. It was established on December 13, 1808, and Huntsville is its seat.

The housing stock matters when you sell. The 2020 census shows 169,820 housing units, about 7.1% of them vacant, and 33.7% of occupied homes are rented. Redstone Arsenal and the space and defense contractors around it have fed the area's job growth since the 1950s, and the population climbed from 72,903 in 1950 to 388,153 by 2020.

A deed for a Madison County house is not always straightforward. Houses inherited through an estate, homes with tenants, and properties with unpaid taxes all need extra steps, and the probate office is where those steps end.

What documents does a probate-related sale usually need in Madison County?

The probate judge's office handles estates as well as land records, so an heir selling an inherited house may deal with both desks. Ask the office or an attorney which estate papers apply to your situation.

  • The prior deed or title information showing how the owner held the property.
  • Any estate paperwork the office or your attorney says applies, when the owner has died.
  • The deed itself, with preparer details and grantor marital status.
  • The RT-1 or matching price language in the deed.
  • Payment for the recording fee and deed tax.

We buy houses in Madison County as they are, including inherited and tax-delinquent homes.

More questions about Madison County, AL Judge of Probate

Where do I record a deed in Madison County, AL?

At the Judge of Probate in the Madison County Service Center, 1918 Memorial Parkway NW, Huntsville, or electronically through an approved vendor such as Simplifile or CSC.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Madison County?

The posted schedule is $25.75 for the first page and $2.50 for each additional page, plus deed tax. The schedule is dated April 1, 2013, so confirm current charges with the office.

What is the Alabama deed tax?

$0.50 per $500 of value or fraction, which is $1.00 per $1,000, under Code of Alabama section 40-22-1. The minimum is $0.50.

Do I need an RT-1 form in Madison County?

Yes, unless the same information is written into the deed. The form carries an extra $2.50 page fee and does not apply to correction deeds.

Can the probate office help me write a deed?

No. The office says its staff are prohibited by law from giving legal advice, so use an attorney or closing agent.

Who records deeds in Jefferson County

  • Probate Court of Jefferson County records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Recording fees (effective 6/1/2012): $16.00 first page plus $3.00 each additional page; $1.00 'No Tax Collected' stamp; $1.00 per additional grantee/grantor beyond 2 each; Deed tax $0.50 per $500; Mortgage tax $0.15 per $100

Jefferson County by the numbers

What does the Jefferson County Judge of Probate do for a home sale?

The Judge of Probate in Jefferson County runs the recording office where deeds and mortgages become part of the public record. When a house sells, the deed goes to this office, the deed tax is collected, and the transfer shows up in the land records.

The same court also handles estates, which is why an inherited house often passes through the same building twice, first for the estate and later for the sale. The office does not give legal advice, and its own FAQ says employees cannot prepare or revise a deed. It points people to an attorney instead.

Where are the two Jefferson County probate offices?

Jefferson County has two probate divisions, one in Birmingham and one in Bessemer. Both work under the same Probate Judge, Deputy Probate Judge and Chief Clerk, and the FAQ lists hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.

DivisionCourthouse address
Birmingham716 North Richard Arrington Jr. Blvd., Birmingham, AL 35203
Bessemer1801 3rd Avenue North, Bessemer, AL 35020

Bessemer is about 16 miles by car southwest of Birmingham. If you are unsure which office to use, call the Probate Court at (205) 325-5203.

How big is Jefferson County, and what is in it?

Jefferson County is the most populous county in Alabama, with 674,721 people in the 2020 census and a 2025 estimate of 665,742. The Legislature created it on December 13, 1819 and named it for Thomas Jefferson.

It covers about 1,124 square miles and lies in the Ridge-and-Valley Appalachians. Shades Mountain is the high point at 1,150 feet, and Red Mountain runs south of downtown Birmingham and separates the city from Homewood. The county sits at the center of what used to be the iron, coal and limestone mining belt of the South, and Birmingham grew out of that industry from about 1871.

Cities in the county include Birmingham, Bessemer, Hoover, Homewood, Vestavia Hills, Mountain Brook, Trussville, Gardendale, Fultondale, Hueytown, Pleasant Grove and Center Point, among others. Several of them reach across county lines. Birmingham, Hoover, Helena, Vestavia Hills, Leeds and Trussville all extend partly into a neighboring county, so confirm which county's records hold your parcel before you start.

What does it cost to record a deed in Jefferson County?

The main state charge is a deed tax of 50 cents for each $500 of value, set by Code of Alabama section 40-22-1. On a $200,000 sale that works out to $200, before any reduction for a mortgage on which the mortgage tax was already paid. Recording fees for the pages themselves come on top, and the office says fees vary by document.

The statute adds several rules worth knowing:

  • A deed must come with proof of the actual purchase price, using the Department of Revenue form.
  • If proof is withheld after a request, the penalty is $100 or 25 percent of the tax, whichever is greater.
  • Two thirds of the tax goes to the state treasury and one third to the county.
  • Deeds for nominal consideration meant only to perfect title carry no tax, and the office stamps them "No Tax Collected."

Ask the closing attorney or title company for the exact total on your settlement statement. Who pays the deed tax is a matter of the sales contract.

What can the recording office tell me, and what can it not?

It can show you the public record, but it cannot tell you whether a lien sits on your house. The FAQ says clerks cannot run a title search, which is a job for a title company or attorney.

Records are open to the public online and in person. Subscribers to the LANDMARK WEB service can search land records and view images of select documents, and clerks offer free on-site training. Many documents can be viewed on the website at no charge, with uncertified printouts for a small fee.

ServiceCost from the FAQ
Copies made in the Record Room$1.00 per page
Plat copies$15.00 per page
Certification of a copy$2.00 more per document

Payment can be made by credit card, cash, cashier's check, money order, business check or local personal check with identification.

What documents does a Jefferson County seller need ready?

  • The deed or estate paperwork showing how you took title.
  • A payoff statement for every mortgage on the house.
  • Government ID for everyone signing.
  • The sales contract, because the price drives the deed tax and the required value statement.
  • Any divorce decree or court order that affects title, since decrees are recorded and indexed with the land records, though not every court document is filed there.

A house owned by a deceased relative needs the estate sorted out first. The buyer's title company will want to see who has authority to sign.

How does the deed record connect to Jefferson County property tax?

Recording the deed is the first of three steps the county revenue offices expect from a new owner. Lauderdale County's published guidance, which follows state practice, says to record the deed in probate court, then assess the property in your name at the revenue office, then claim any exemption.

The state says property taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. Because the bill tracks the owner of record from the prior October 1, the first bill after a sale can still carry the seller's name. Sellers who see a bill after closing should send it to the title company or the buyer.

What do Jefferson County sellers commonly face?

The county is large and varied, so the problems vary with the neighborhood.

  • Older homes in former mill and mining communities, such as Ensley, North Birmingham and Woodlawn, which were once separate towns and are now Birmingham neighborhoods.
  • Inherited houses where heirs live out of state.
  • Parcels near county lines where it is unclear which probate office applies.
  • Vacant houses with unpaid tax or code issues.
  • Sellers who need to close fast and cannot wait for a retail buyer's financing.

Cash Home Buyers makes written offers on Jefferson County houses as they stand, and the closing goes through a local title company that handles the recording.

How is Jefferson County governed?

The county is run by a five-member commission, with each commissioner elected from a single-member district. Jefferson County has limited home rule, which lets it handle zoning, sewers, highways and trash collection, though the list the county gives for those powers leaves out property taxes.

The county's sewer financing produced a well-known crisis. Costs rose sharply, rates grew more than 300 percent over 15 years before 2011, and the county declared bankruptcy in 2011. This is old news for most sellers, but it explains why you may hear sewer charges discussed in older neighborhoods.

More questions about Jefferson County, AL Judge of Probate

Where do I record a deed in Jefferson County, Alabama?

Record it with the Probate Court of Jefferson County, at the Birmingham division (716 North Richard Arrington Jr. Blvd.) or the Bessemer division (1801 3rd Avenue North). Hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.

How much is the Alabama deed tax?

Alabama charges 50 cents per $500 of value, or fraction of $500, under Code of Alabama section 40-22-1. On a $200,000 sale that is $200, less any reduction for a mortgage on which mortgage tax was paid.

Can the Jefferson County probate office prepare my deed?

No. The office says employees may not prepare or revise a deed or give legal advice, and it suggests contacting an attorney.

Can the recording office tell me if there is a lien on my house?

No. Clerks cannot perform a title search, so a title company or attorney has to do it.

How much does a copy of a recorded deed cost?

Copies made in the Record Room are $1.00 per page, plats are $15.00 per page, and certification costs $2.00 more per document.

Do I need to prove the sale price when recording?

Yes. Alabama requires proof of the actual purchase price or value, using the Department of Revenue form. Withholding it after a request can bring a penalty of $100 or 25 percent of the tax.

Who records deeds in Shelby County

  • Shelby County Probate Court records deeds and mortgages.

Fees

Selling in Shelby County?

Shelby County by the numbers

What does the Shelby County judge of probate do when a house is sold?

The judge of probate is the county officer who takes a signed deed into the public record and collects the state's recordation tax on it. Alabama's section 40-22-1 says a deed or similar instrument cannot be received for record until the privilege tax is paid.

The Department of Revenue tells new owners to record the deed in the probate office and then assess the property at the county revenue office, bringing the deed along. For a Shelby County sale, that means two stops after closing: probate for the record, then the property tax office for the assessment.

We could not open the Shelby County government pages for the probate fee schedule, hours or e-recording rules, so none of those are listed here. Call the office or read its current fee sheet before you plan a closing date.

How is the deed tax figured on a Shelby County deed?

The tax is 50 cents for every $500 of value conveyed, or fraction of $500, and it is figured on the actual price paid. Under section 40-22-1(c), only the value above a mortgage or vendor's lien that has already paid mortgage tax is taxable.

The deed must arrive with proof of the real price, on a form the Department of Revenue develops, and the person signing attests that it is accurate in good faith. If no proof is given, the judge of probate bases the tax on the latest assessed value and adds a penalty. The statute sets that penalty at $100 or 25 percent of the tax actually due, whichever is greater, for someone who intentionally withholds proof after being asked.

ItemWhat section 40-22-1 says
Rate$0.50 per $500 of value or fraction
Tax baseActual price, less mortgage or lien that paid mortgage tax
Split of the taxTwo thirds to the state, one third to the county
Penalty for withheld proof$100 or 25 percent of tax due, whichever is greater
No tax requiredNominal-consideration title-perfecting deeds, corrected deeds, mortgage transfers that already paid

Which deeds are exempt, and what happens to a deed that spans two counties?

Several instruments carry no recordation tax. The statute lists deeds written for nominal consideration to perfect title, the re-recording of corrected instruments, and transfers of mortgages on which the mortgage tax was paid. When a deed is exempt, the judge of probate stamps it "No Tax Collected."

A deed covering land in two or more counties follows a separate route. The probate judge certifies the instrument to the Department of Revenue, which sets the value in each county. The filer can deposit an estimated amount to get the deed recorded right away, and any excess is refunded once the value is fixed.

That rule matters in Shelby County because several places straddle county lines. Vestavia Hills, Hoover, Helena, Leeds and Calera are each partly in another county, per the county's Wikipedia entry. A title company will check whether your parcel sits entirely inside one county.

Where is Shelby County and how big is it?

Shelby County sits in central Alabama, and its county seat is Columbiana. Wikipedia's county entry gives a total area of 810 square miles, 785 of them land, and names Alabaster as the largest city.

The county was established on February 7, 1818, and named for Isaac Shelby. The first seat was Shelbyville, in what is now Pelham. The seat moved to Columbia, now Columbiana, in 1826, and the current limestone courthouse was built from 1905 to 1906. The 1854 brick courthouse is now the Shelby County Museum and Archives.

Shelby County borders six other counties:

  • St. Clair County to the northeast
  • Talladega County to the east
  • Coosa County to the southeast
  • Chilton County to the south
  • Bibb County to the southwest
  • Jefferson County to the northwest

How fast has Shelby County grown?

Shelby County's population grew from 66,298 in 1980 to 223,024 in 2020, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 238,552. For the 2020 census the county had 84,241 households and 89,060 housing units, and 78.1 percent of occupied homes were owner-occupied.

Growth followed the roads. Interstate 65 and U.S. 31 link the county to Jefferson County, and Wikipedia ties suburban growth in Pelham, Helena, Alabaster and Chelsea to that access. Other major routes are U.S. 231, U.S. 280 and several state roads.

The county's economy was farm-based for a long time. Wikipedia says soybeans have passed cotton as the main crop since about 1990, and that the county once hosted an early inland waterway on the Coosa River and an early east-west railroad. The county page lists CSX, Norfolk Southern and the Calera and Shelby Railroad among its railroads.

For a seller, the practical advice is to bring a signed deed, a correct legal description and a completed value form, because a deed that needs corrections costs time at the counter.

What land and schools define Shelby County?

The county is partly hilly and partly flat. Oak Mountain and Double Oak Mountain are the southern tail of the Appalachians, while much of the rest is farmland and pasture with lowlands along two rivers. The Cahaba River runs along the northern edge and the Coosa River valley takes in the east. Lay Lake is a large reservoir that borders Shelby and three other counties.

Schools are split among several systems. Shelby County Schools serves areas outside Hoover, Alabaster and Pelham, while Alabaster City Schools, Pelham City Schools and Hoover City Schools serve their own cities. Higher education includes the University of Montevallo and a Jefferson State Community College campus.

If you own property near a lake, river or the Cahaba, ask your insurer and the county about flood maps before you list. We did not find county flood zone figures on a page we could open, so none are given here.

What do Shelby County sellers run into at the probate office?

The common snags are about the paper, not the house. Watch for these:

  • A deed that names the wrong legal description or a misspelled owner, which may need a corrected deed.
  • No proof of the purchase price, which triggers the value penalty.
  • An unpaid property tax bill, since Alabama taxes turn delinquent after December 31.
  • An owner who has died, where the estate may need a court order before the house can be conveyed.

Alabama counties are not required to mail tax notices, so an owner who never received a bill is still responsible. A buyer should check payment status with the county before the deed is recorded.

Cash buyers pay the same tax and the same recording costs as anyone else. What a cash sale changes is the repair list and the wait for a buyer's lender, not the recording steps.

More questions about Shelby County, AL Judge of Probate

Who records deeds in Shelby County, Alabama?

The judge of probate. The Alabama Department of Revenue tells buyers to record the deed in the probate office and then assess the property at the county revenue office.

What is the Alabama deed tax rate?

Fifty cents for each $500 of value conveyed, or fraction of $500, under section 40-22-1, less any mortgage or lien that already paid mortgage tax. Two thirds goes to the state and one third to the county.

Do I need to show the sale price when I record a Shelby County deed?

Yes. The deed must come with proof of the actual purchase price, using a Department of Revenue form. Intentionally withholding it after a request carries a penalty of $100 or 25 percent of the tax, whichever is greater.

Is any deed recorded without tax?

Some are. Deeds for nominal consideration that perfect title, corrected deeds and mortgage transfers that already paid tax are listed as exceptions, and the probate judge stamps them "No Tax Collected."

What are the recording fees in Shelby County?

We could not open the county's fee schedule, so we are not quoting a number. Ask the Shelby County probate office for the current schedule before closing.
